instruction: Set the system timezone to New York (US Eastern).

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened GNOME Settings, navigated to Date & Time, opened the timezone map picker, searched for 'London', and changed timezone from HKT (UTC+8) to GMT (UTC+0) in 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open GNOME Settings, navigate sidebar sections, interact with Date & Time settings, use timezone map search, select timezone from results, modify system settings
metadata.task_rationale: Agent demonstrated the exact workflow of searching for and selecting a timezone. This variation uses the same pattern but targets a different timezone (New York instead of London), testing generalization of the timezone-change capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing system timezone to US Eastern (America/New_York). Evaluator checks timedatectl output includes 'America/New_York'. Same interaction pattern as original task but with a different target city.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'timedatectl status' to extract current timezone state, which outputs the timezone identifier (e.g., 'Time zone: America/New_York (EST, -0500)')
Metric 'check_include_exclude' correctly checks if 'America/New_York' is contained in the timedatectl output string

Parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly to the metric, and check_include_exclude accesses rules.get('include') and rules.get('exclude') correctly
Expected value 'America/New_York' is the correct IANA timezone identifier for US Eastern Time
Single instruction requirement (set timezone to New York) is fully covered by the evaluator
